description: The ordinary hardfork: one chain, one build at a time. Four stablenet producers run the pre-fork build, every node is stopped well before the boho block, and all four come back on the build that knows boho — same chain, same databases, same work, a different executable. The fork then swaps govMinter to v2, which is what proves the restarted network crossed rather than merely bounced. It also proves the new build was needed: with the pre-fork build on both sides the network does not start at all, because that build has no BohoBlock to configure. The go-wemix cases prove the other shape, where two sets of nodes run at once and production changes hands.
